en: (The number one regional magazine in the Tokai area. It's well known for its details on the best driving courses, popular dishes, places to visit, and restaurants.)
(An entertainment magazine that talks about events, grubs, day trip hot springs, driving roads, movies, television shows, and music.)
(The top magazine in the Kyushu/Yamaguchi area. Includes plenty of ideas on food, entertainment, leisure, and suggested trips to take.)
(A lifestyle magazine published by Shufu to Seikatsusha. A bible for those mature men who want a dash of bad boy flair, and offers fashion advice for casual and formal attire.)

(An old town magazine, in print since 1976. It's well known for its popular character, Fukuoka-ojisan. Leave it to this magazine for entertainment, foods, and all the intel you'll ever need on Fukuoka.)
(A magazine published by M-ON! Entertainment Inc. that talks about the newest digital items. A representative for each category gives information about a product they recommend.)
(Fusosha's weekly magazine, targeted at white-collar workers. It appeals to young men with its ambitious features and series of topical articles.)
(A biweekly TV guide published by the Tokyo News Service. It's popular for its articles, such as in-depth features for avid fans, plus up-to-date programming schedules.)
(Takeshobo's monthly mahjong manga magazine. Its many famous manga series are full of thrilling mahjong battles that leave readers on the edge of their seats.)
(A weekly magazine for men published by the Nihon Journal. Provides a wealth of information on male-oriented entertainment and features columns that take a critical look at Japanese society.)
(A renowned gaming magazine published by Enterbrain. Chock full of game reviews, articles, reader polls, and more.)
(That's enough magazine reading for now.)
(Probably shouldn't spend all day in front of the magazine stand.)
(Had enough lookin' at these things.)
(I think I'm good for now.)
(That was fun. Maybe I'll come back to read some more later!)

Yo, Ta-chan. Interview?
Oh, hi. Yeah. I'm running late, though.

Listen, you gotta write about us again. We got clients
singing our praises left and right because they read your
article. Seems like people still have faith in print media.
Yeah? That's great. I'll take it up with the editor-in-chief soon, promise. Gotta go!
Brings back memories, don't it? Of course, I was always a backup in high school. I never got to pitch a game.
That's right. You were a pitcher, too. When it came to raw power, I thought you outclassed even Shirakawa. And he was the best of the best.
But high school ball is all about winning tournaments. No coach would rely on a pitcher who would melt down on walks.
It didn't matter how hard I threw⑬the pitchers who got to play were guys like Shirakawa. Guys with good control.
Yeah, I guess...
In the summer of our senior year, when we finally made it to Koshien, our team got a lot of attention. You especially, since you batted cleanup.
I had to watch you guys in the spotlight from the shadows right nearby. It made it all the more pathetic, being so close to the light.
I had to cheer for you guys on the field in a game I wouldn't get to play. Up in the stands with everyone else in faraway Koshien.
Did I go through all that tough training just so I could make you guys look good? That was always gnawing at my soul.
After spending my teens in sweat and grime, I ended up with nothing.
It didn't take long for me to hate baseball. I felt like I wasted my youth.
What are you trying to say, Kurosaki? Are you blaming us for the way your life turned out?
Get in the batter's box, Shinada. My pitching against your batting. That's how we'll settle the score.
What are you trying to prove?
That we're not so different, you and I. Whatever happened in the past be damned.
I'm not the only one to be ruined by baseball. You got tarred and feathered by the pros⑬you should loathe baseball just as much as I do.
Speak for yourself.
Oh, right. You're the one in the spotlight's shadow now. You might be desperate to forget that, but I'll make you remember!
Fine. I'll show you we're nothing alike.
You still got it, Shinada. I lost, fair and square.
You won't be seeing me again, either. I'm skipping town.
To be honest, my broker business was screwed a long time ago. It's like everything else for me⑬it all turns to shit.
Worse yet, I got too aggressive, and ended up drawing attention from some yakuza. So I have to disappear before they do it for me.
Well, you brought this all on yourself. Don't look at me for sympathy.
I know that. I was planning to get out of the business anyway. You just moved the timing up a little, is all.
Hey, Kurosaki. Why didn't you cut and run already? Why bother coming to me for this?
So I can finally be rid of baseball for good. I despised it all this time. I wanted to be done with it properly, that's all.
Quit lying, man.
Lying? You lost me there.
Look, no one who hates baseball could ever pitch like that. Even after high school, you kept working on your throw, didn't you?
Why would you lie to yourself just to hide the pain? It only gets worse that way.
...Maybe you have a point.
Take this. For your trouble.
Look after Shirakawa, will you? He's just like me⑬stuck in the past, unable to move on with his life.
Yeah. I know.
Heh. Looks like our team was full of problem kids. Give it up for ol' West Kamuro.
(Shirakawa. There's that score to settle, too.)
Hmph. If that's the best you can do, you're dead meat against Shirakawa.
You don't have a chance of beating him if you can't get through me first.
Let's go, Shinada. My pitching or your batting. Let's see which holds up.
Fine by me. Bring it on, Kurosaki!
Will this do? You had it out with Kurosaki here, didn't you?
Huh, he actually told you? He asked me to look after you, you know.
Hmph. What could he possibly ask you to do?
Atone for your twenty-year-old crime? For robbing me of baseball so you could satisfy your pride?
You won't listen to anything I say, will you? Not until I hit an Akamatsu pitch. Though I doubt you can throw one in this state.
Your shoulder's messed up, man. Blown. Torn. Injured. How many ways must I say it?
I admit my left shoulder will never be the same. But I still have my right shoulder.
You're gonna throw right? What are you thinking? There's no way you'll beat me with an overnight conversion.
It's not an overnight conversion. I switched to throwing right after I saw you hit that homer on a stolen sign.
